title: Backlog items record the operator id: a sprint's creator and owner, a claim's operator and the operator who answered a gate
goal: backlog.py new sprint records the operator id of kbwho.operator() as the sprint's creator; set SP --owner ID --by operator records its owner and refuses a value shaped like an email address; claim records the operator id beside claimed_by; an answer --by operator records the operator id and the answering session's role on the gate beside by, and gate classes and who may answer stay as they are; backlog.py check accepts the creator, owner and operator fields and refuses one that holds an email address

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print("check failed:", e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import os, shutil, subprocess, tempfile, json, re
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
C = os.path.join(T, "clone")
shutil.copytree("_tools", os.path.join(C, "_tools"), ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__", "*.pyc", "fixtures"))
shutil.copytree(".claude/hooks", os.path.join(C, ".claude", "hooks"))
for f in ("backlog.json", ".gitignore"):
    shutil.copy(f, C)
os.makedirs(os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog"))
shutil.copy("kb/_self/map.csv", os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "map.csv"))
B = os.path.join(T, "bin"); os.makedirs(B)
EM = "jan.kowalski" + chr(64) + "corp-mail.test"  # built at run time: no address sits in the check's text
def stub(body):
    p = os.path.join(B, "claude"); open(p, "w").write("#!/bin/sh\n" + body + "\n"); os.chmod(p, 0o755)
stub("echo '{\"loggedIn\": true, \"authMethod\": \"claude.ai\", \"email\": \"%s\"}'" % EM)
ENV = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(("GIT_", "KB_", "CLAUDE"))}
ENV.update(PATH=os.pathsep.join([B, os.path.dirname(shutil.which("git")), "/usr/bin", "/bin"]), HOME=T,
           GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1", KB_LIVE_DOCS="0", KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(T, "coord.sqlite"),
           GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="t@example.com", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="t@example.com")
def g(*a):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=C, env=ENV, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
def run(tool, *a, stdin=None, **kw):
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(C, *tool.split("/")) if "/" in tool else os.path.join(C, "_tools", tool), *a],
                          cwd=C, env={**ENV, **kw}, input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
g("init", "-q", "-b", "main"); g("add", "-A"); g("commit", "-qm", "base")
O = dict(KB_OPERATOR="op-test0001", KB_ROLE="orchestrator")
item = lambda i: json.load(open(os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog", i + ".json")))
r = run("backlog.py", "new", "sprint", "--title", "Planted", "--goal", "a planted goal", **O)
sp = re.search(r"new sprint (SP-\w+)", r.stdout).group(1)
assert item(sp).get("creator") == "op-test0001", ("a new sprint does not record its creator", item(sp))
run("backlog.py", "answer", sp, "start", "--answer", "approve", "--by", "operator", **O)
gt = [x for x in item(sp)["gates"] if x["id"] == "start"][0]
assert (gt.get("by"), gt.get("operator"), gt.get("role")) == ("operator", "op-test0001", "orchestrator"), ("an operator's gate answer does not record the operator id and role", gt)
r = run("backlog.py", "set", sp, "--owner", "op-own00002", "--by", "operator", **O)
assert r.returncode == 0 and item(sp).get("owner") == "op-own00002", ("set --owner does not record the owner", r.returncode, r.stderr[-300:])
r = run("backlog.py", "set", sp, "--owner", EM, "--by", "operator", **O)
assert r.returncode != 0 and item(sp).get("owner") == "op-own00002", ("set --owner takes an email address", r.returncode, item(sp).get("owner"))
r = run("backlog.py", "new", "story", "--title", "Planted claim", "--goal", "a planted claim", "--sprint", sp, "--touch", "kb/x.md",
        "--check", "python3 _tools/backlog.py config", **O)
s = re.search(r"new story (ST-\w+)", r.stdout).group(1)
run("backlog.py", "start", sp, **O)
r = run("backlog.py", "claim", s, "--by", "w1", KB_OPERATOR="op-wkr00003", KB_ROLE="worker")
it = item(s)
assert it.get("claimed_by") == "w1" and it.get("operator") == "op-wkr00003", ("a claim does not record the operator beside claimed_by", r.stderr[-300:], it)
r = run("backlog.py", "check", **O)
assert r.returncode == 0, ("backlog.py check refuses the operator fields", r.stdout[-500:])
p = os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog", sp + ".json"); d = json.load(open(p)); d["creator"] = EM; json.dump(d, open(p, "w"), indent=2)
r = run("backlog.py", "check", **O)
assert r.returncode != 0 and sp in r.stdout + r.stderr, ("backlog.py check accepts an email address as creator", r.stdout[-300:])

gates.question: What does a gate answered --by operator record beside by, so that an answer an orchestrator gave on the operator's delegation is told apart from one the operator typed?
options: the operator id and the answering session's role (interactive, orchestrator or worker)
gates.recommendation: the operator id and the answering session's role (interactive, orchestrator or worker)
gates.answer: the operator id and the answering session's role (interactive, orchestrator or worker)

notes: Premise (2026-10-19): in a planted backlog, new sprint writes no creator, claim writes no operator, an operator's gate answer records by only, and set has no --owner flag. kb/_self/map.csv maps _tools/bl_base.py to kb/_self/querylog.md: a field list change there is reviewed against it; the query log's own fields are another item's open gate. Test policy (D-6kei5o2z, D-2tq4fhgs): no new test or test file; the check is a tool run on a throwaway clone built from this checkout's _tools and .claude/hooks with its own coord store and a stub claude on PATH; no change to _tools/tests_ceiling.json. Design: kb/_self/design.md, Teams and organizations; facts: public/claude/ci-and-headless.md:124-127, public/claude/otel-monitoring.md:51-53, QK-claude-code-session-learn-email-account. Addresses in checks are built at run time; docs and items use the placeholder jan.kowalski only.
